assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a single superconducting artificial atom and a single microwave photon interact in the strong-coupling regime on a chip, with dispersive readout and control. It opened a new regime of controllable light-matter physics and became the standard architecture for superconducting qubits, entangling gates and quantum-limited measurement. The discovery is the physics of strong coupling, not the application, which suits the prize criteria. It follows naturally on the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf are the usual core, with the 2004 theory proposal (Blais) and the first experiment (Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues). Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf form a clean three-person configuration. Credit to Girvin and Devoret for the broader Yale programme is a possible dispute, though the supplied names support a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and extended in dozens of laboratories for two decades. The interpretation is stable and the platform is in daily use for photon-number resolution, QND readout and multi-qubit processors. Recognition is timely, and arguably slightly overdue.
uncertainties: Whether Devoret's, Girvin's or others' roles should be recognised is outside the supplied credited names.
I work in this area and know some of these groups, so my own judgement may be biased; I rely on recall, not independent verification of dates and priorities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting and observing the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator opened a whole class of matter characterised by topology, with robust edge and surface states. The idea was original and the experimental confirmation in HgTe was clean. It has had very broad influence across condensed matter and beyond, including topological superconductivity and Majorana platforms.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory of the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall effect in graphene; Molenkamp led the HgTe experiment with the Zhang theory proposal. Shoucheng Zhang's death means his contribution cannot be recognised, which complicates the picture. The Kane, Mele and Molenkamp triple is coherent. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe proposal and Fu and Kane's 3D generalisation are partly outside this credit set.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups through transport and ARPES, including three-dimensional topological insulators. The field is mature and stable, and recognition is timely, if not late. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and TKNN-type phases, so a committee must judge how distinct this is.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz) may reduce perceived novelty.
Credit division with Fu, Bernevig, Hughes and the late Shoucheng Zhang, which cannot all be reflected in three names.
Not my area of strongest expertise, so I defer partly to condensed-matter colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire materials field. It is an original, surprising discovery that gave a tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological physics, with rapid and wide impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero and colleagues made the 2018 experiments. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing and fits three laureates. Cao, Fatemi and others (first authors of the experiment) are not eligible within the supplied names, and Kim, Yacoby and others have important parallel contributions.
assessment.maturity: Broad independent confirmation across laboratories, with an active field. The superconductivity mechanism is still not settled, so the interpretation is only partly stable. Timing is plausible but possibly early for a prize that wants lasting consequence.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity in the magic-angle system is debated.
Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder complicate the reproducibility story.
Contributions of others beyond the supplied names (for example earlier moire band-structure theory) are not captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition for cold atoms in optical lattices and its realisation opened quantum simulation of many-body Hamiltonians with exquisite control. It is a clear case where a basic quantum phenomenon was made visible and tunable, with continuing impact through quantum gas microscopy and Hubbard-model studies.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller theory proposal and Greiner-Bloch observation are the pivotal steps; Cirac and Zoller are the principal theoretical architects of the quantum-simulation programme. Greiner's contribution is the first experiment and a case could be made for him, but with the three-name limit I propose Bloch, Cirac and Zoller. Jaksch, Hansch and others have claims too, so the allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed in many laboratories over more than twenty years. Quantum simulation advantage claims for specific problems are still developing, but the underlying physics results are solid. Recognition is plausible and timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2001 BEC and 2012 prizes on controlled quantum systems may weigh against.
Contested credit between theory and experiment, including Greiner, Jaksch, Hansch and Bloch's own group.
Cirac and Zoller also appear in other entries, so the committee must avoid double counting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Electron spins in gate-defined quantum dots were proposed as qubits and then realised, with single-spin readout, coherent control and high-fidelity two-qubit gates, including in silicon and germanium. It is a strong basis for semiconductor quantum computing and a clear case of foundational quantum measurement becoming a platform, but the key discoveries are partly engineering milestones.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo made the 1998 proposal (DiVincenzo is not in this entry); Tarucha, Vandersypen, Kouwenhoven and others achieved the experimental steps. Credit allocation is complicated by overlap with another entry that credits Bruce Kane and DiVincenzo, and Kouwenhoven and Petta are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experimental progress is steady and independent, with silicon spin qubits now showing fidelities above 99 percent, though the route to scale is still unproven. Recognition may be somewhat premature compared with superconducting or trapped-ion platforms.
uncertainties: Credit split with DiVincenzo, Kane, Kouwenhoven and Petta is unresolved.
The scalability of the platform remains unproven, which a wary committee would weigh.
There is a competing duplicate entry on spin-qubit proposals in the longlist.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ground-state cooling and quantum control of mechanical resonators, from sideband cooling to the quantum regime in both optomechanical and piezoelectric circuit systems, demonstrated quantum behaviour in macroscopic objects. This is conceptually close to the 2025 theme and connects to my own work on phonons coupled to artificial atoms. It is a clean demonstration that opened a new regime.
assessment.attribution: Cleland (quantum ground state and single-phonon control in a superconducting-circuit platform), Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg (cavity optomechanics, strong coupling and cooling) are distinct but complementary routes. O'Connell, Teufel, Lehnert and Painter also made decisive steps, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by several groups, and the field is robust. Applications to sensing and transduction are still emerging. The foundational result is mature but there is no single clean breakthrough event, which makes timing uncertain.
uncertainties: Split of credit between optomechanics and circuit electromechanics routes is unclear.
Teufel, Lehnert, Painter and O'Connell are not in the credited set.
Impact on fundamental physics is less direct than for the top candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable arrays of individually trapped Rydberg atoms with tweezer control enable strongly interacting quantum simulation and gates with large qubit numbers, including new many-body phases and logical-qubit demonstrations. It is exciting and fast moving, with important physics results.
assessment.attribution: Saffman contributed the Rydberg-blockade gate proposals, Browaeys the early demonstrations of blockade and spin models, and Lukin the large programmable arrays and many-body experiments. Bernien, Greiner, Endres, Weiss and Jaksch are among others with notable contributions, so a three-person division is hard.
assessment.maturity: Moving quickly and confirmed by several groups, but the field is young, and the scientific interpretation of what will remain central is not yet settled. Recognition now seems premature compared with older platforms.
uncertainties: Premature relative to the long-term significance; leading results are recent.
Credit allocation among many contributors is contested.
Lukin also appears in the colour-centre entry, so the committee must consider his total standing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error-correcting codes showed that fragile quantum information can be protected, and the fault-tolerance framework underlies all scalable quantum computing. The idea is original and fundamental, and recent experiments with surface codes below threshold begin to demonstrate it. As a theorist I value it highly, but I also note that it is quantum information science and mathematics more than physics discovery.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane gave the first codes in 1995-96; Kitaev contributed the toric code and fault-tolerant anyon ideas. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme, Preskill and others contributed to code theory and threshold results, so a three-person allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstration is recent (superconducting surface-code results beyond break-even) and full-scale fault tolerance is still ahead. This is a strong long-term candidate but likely early for recognition, in line with the cautious view that the promise has not yet been delivered.
uncertainties: Fault-tolerant quantum computing has not yet been demonstrated at scale.
Fit to a physics prize is debatable, since much of the work is theoretical computer science.
Attribution to three people omits several important contributors (Gottesman, Calderbank, Knill, Laflamme, Preskill).
